# 1 Clement Chapter 4 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalence)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_004_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 4

**4:1** For it is written thus: "And it came to pass after certain days that Cain brought from the fruits of the earth a sacrifice to God, and Abel also brought from the firstborn of his flock and of their fat portions. And God looked upon Abel and his gifts, but upon Cain and his sacrifices he did not look. And Cain was very sorrowful and his countenance fell." [Gen 4:3-5 LXX]

**4:2** "And God said to Cain: 'Why are you very sorrowful, and why has your countenance fallen? If you have offered rightly but have not rightly divided, have you not sinned? Be at peace; his recourse is to you, and you shall have dominion over him.'" [Gen 4:6-7 LXX]

**4:3** "And Cain said to Abel his brother: 'Let us go into the field.' And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother and killed him." [Gen 4:8 LXX]

**4:4** You see, brothers, jealousy and envy wrought a fratricide.

**4:5** On account of jealousy our father Jacob fled from the face of his brother Esau. [Gen 27:41ff]

**4:6** Jealousy was the cause of Joseph being persecuted unto near death and being sold into bondage. [Gen 37]

**4:7** Jealousy compelled Moses to flee from the face of Pharaoh king of Egypt, when he heard from his own kinsman: "Who appointed you a ruler and a judge over us? Do you wish to kill me as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?" [Exod 2:14 LXX]

**4:8** On account of jealousy Aaron and Miriam were excluded outside the camp. [Num 12:14-15]

**4:9** Jealousy sent Dathan and Abiram down alive into Hades, because they rose up in sedition against Moses the servant of God. [Num 16:33]

**4:10** On account of jealousy David not only met with envy from foreigners, but also endured persecution from Saul the king of Israel. [1 Sam 18:6ff]

---

*LOGOS formal equivalence translation, with LXX citations carefully preserved.*
